extracted.intended_audience: general public, stakeholders, and Federal agencies invited to comment on the Census Bureau's information collection (ACS Methods Panel Tests); survey researchers and practitioners interested in ACS testing
extracted.subtask_short: comment on ACS methods panel ICR
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting public comments in response to the Census Bureau's Federal Register notice requesting review and comment on the proposed American Community Survey Methods Panel Tests information collection (ICR) under the Paperwork Reduction Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments must be received by deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure consideration, comments regarding this proposed information collection must be received on or before December 23, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received after this date may not be considered. (Document states: 'To ensure consideration, comments ... must be received on or before December 23, 2024.')

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written comments by email to acso.pra@census.gov or via the Federal e-Rulemaking Portal (www.regulations.gov) using the 'Comment Now!' icon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting, reference 'American Community Survey Methods Panel Tests' in the email subject line or identify comments by Docket Number USBC-2024-0027 on Regulations.gov; complete required fields when using the portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted attachment formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments to electronic comments may be submitted in Microsoft Word, Excel, or Adobe PDF file formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If attaching files to electronic comments via Regulations.gov or email, use .doc/.docx, .xls/.xlsx, or .pdf formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record and PII caution
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received are part of the public record and may be publicly accessible; personally identifiable information voluntarily submitted may be accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit Confidential Business Information or otherwise sensitive or protected information. You may request withholding of personal identifying information, but the agency cannot guarantee it will be withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review, redaction, and posting of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments will generally be posted without change after the comment period has closed; however, the agency may withhold or redact content prior to posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited evaluation criterion — practical utility / necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposed information collection is necessary for the proper functions of the Department, including whether the information will have practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should explain how the collection supports the Department's functions and provide evidence or argument about practical uses of the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited evaluation criterion — accuracy of burden estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy of the estimate of the time and cost burden for this proposed collection, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or reasoned critique of respondent counts, time-per-response estimates, cost assumptions, and the methodology used to produce burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited evaluation criterion — enhance quality, utility, clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend question wording changes, formats, modes, or collection procedures that would improve data quality, clarity for respondents, and usefulness of resulting statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited evaluation criterion — minimize reporting burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate ways to minimize the reporting burden on those who are to respond, including the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest alternatives to reduce respondent time, number of contacts, or reliance on burdensome response modes; propose automation or administrative record use where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent obligation (legal status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Obligation: Mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ICR notes that participation obligations are mandatory under the cited legal authority (see legal authority entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal authority for the collection is Title 13 U.S.C. 141, 193, and 221.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides statutory basis for the Census Bureau's information collection and respondent obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General objective for ACS Methods Panel Tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACS Methods Panel is designed to address emerging survey issues and test methods for reducing data collection costs, addressing respondent burden, improving survey response, data quality, and survey efficiencies for housing units and group quarters, and to test new questions for the Decennial Census Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and evaluations should consider these overarching goals when assessing proposed tests and proposed metrics for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaire Timing Test evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether changing the timing of when the ACS paper questionnaire is sent to sampled addresses increases self-response (overall and by data collection mode) and/or reduces data collection costs; also evaluate impact of including a Quick Response (QR) code directing respondents to the internet instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key outcomes: self-response rates by mode, changes in data collection costs (including reductions in paper-related costs and CAPI nonresponse follow-up), and any mode-shift effects attributable to QR codes or timing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet instrument response option and error message design test criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess response option design (standard radio buttons vs. bordered 'response buttons' with hover and color-change behavior) and error message design changes to determine effects on response time, response distributions, and item nonresponse; and measure respondent reactions to different error displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes include changes in completion time, altered answer distributions, increased/decreased item nonresponse, and qualitative reaction to error cues (colors, arrows vs. border change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional internet instrument testing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Test revisions to internet instrument elements such as login procedures, screen navigation, user interface design, and methods to decrease respondent burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use split-sample experiments and other experimental designs to assess usability and burden; consider device types (smartphones, tablets, desktops) given varying screen sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-response mail messaging and contact strategies testing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate changes to mailings (plain language, visual redesign, motivational messaging), materials included in mailings, contact methods, number of contacts, and timing to see if these changes increase self-response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design split-sample tests on housing units; measure self-response rates, cost per response, and differential effects across populations; test combinations of messaging, visuals, and contact cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content testing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the impact of changing question wording, response categories, or redefining constructs on data quality; for new questions, compare two versions and benchmark against other known sources; measure response bias or variance via follow-up interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct split-sample experiments with follow-up reinterviews to assess measurement error, bias, and variance; compare to benchmarks where available and evaluate across all modes of data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponse follow-up (NRFU) data collection testing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate modifications to NRFU operations, including changes to field representative materials and messaging, types of materials used, contact methods, timing, and other operational approaches to increase response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on in-person and telephone interviews conducted by field representatives, but account for FR encouragement of online response and distribution of materials; measure NRFU response rates and cost impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design criterion — split-sample methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Many tests will be conducted as split-sample experiments (half of sampled addresses receive one version and half receive another) to allow direct comparison of alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs may include split-sample web/instrument variations, mail-contact strategies, and content versions; follow-up reinterviews may be used to measure bias/variance from each arm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of collection and mode-specific inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACS is collected via internet, paper questionnaire, telephone interview, and in-person interview (CAPI); tests will use all or a subset of these modes as appropriate to the test purpose. IVR and TQA provide help but not response via IVR; administrative records may supplement or replace data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which modes are included in each test; recognize that mode affects response behavior and measurement, and that test outcomes must be interpreted in a mode-specific context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimation metrics and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimates of number of respondents, estimated time per response, total burden hours, and estimated total annual cost to the public (indirect costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists respondent counts and minutes per response for each test and reports total burden hours (including annualized figures). Comments should address the validity of these estimates and whether production samples can be used to reduce incremental burden.
